tracks.name: Wimbledon Park Track

mapEmbed.title: Wimbledon Park Track location map

tracks.description: Wimbledon Park Athletics Track is a 400m synthetic track located within the grounds of Wimbledon Park in southwest London. Opened in the early 1950s, it was upgraded from a cinder surface to synthetic in 1990 and underwent major improvements in 2005. The track has six lanes, with an eight-lane home straight, and is equipped for a wide range of track and field events. It is home to Hercules Wimbledon AC and is also used by other local athletics and running groups. Surrounded by the park's greenery, it provides a distinctive setting for athletics in southwest London.

tracks.description: Tooting Bec Athletics Track is a historic athletics venue on Tooting Common in southwest London. Originally opened as a cinder track in 1937, it became one of London's earliest floodlit athletics venues in the late 1940s. The track was converted to a synthetic surface in 1985 and underwent a major £500,000 refurbishment in 2022, when a new Rekortan M surface was installed. The venue features an eight-lane, 400m track, additional sprint lanes and facilities for a wide range of field events. It is home to Herne Hill Harriers and offers a gym, fitness studio and spectator seating.

tracks.description: Canons House and Grounds Track is a historic cinder running track in Mitcham, dating back to the 1920s. Originally part of the News of the World Sports Ground, it was once the home of Mitcham Athletics Club, which trained there until the early 1960s. The track has a notable sporting heritage, with Olympic high-jump medallist Dorothy Tyler among the athletes associated with the venue. Rediscovered and restored in 2020 as part of the Canons House & Grounds heritage project, it is now preserved as a public recreational space, offering a rare glimpse into the history of athletics in Mitcham.

tracks.description: Victoria Park Athletics Arena is a historic cinder running track located within Victoria Park in East London. Built in the early 1920s, it originally featured four lanes, with a fifth lane added later. The track was converted from 440 yards to 400 metres in the early 1970s and became the home of Victoria Park Harriers from 1926 until 2000, when the club moved to the nearby Mile End Stadium. Once a popular venue for athletics meetings attracting large crowds, it is now a relatively basic facility used mainly for casual training. It remains one of London's few surviving cinder tracks.

The stadium features an eight-lane, 400m synthetic track, floodlighting, a covered sprint straight and facilities for a wide range of field events. It is home to Thames Valley Harriers and has a long tradition of hosting club, regional and national athletics competitions.

tracks.description: Osterley Sports and Athletics Centre is a community athletics venue in Isleworth, west London. The current six-lane, 400m synthetic track opened in 2010, replacing an unusual three-lane track that had previously occupied the site. The earlier facility had itself evolved from a six-lane cinder track dating back to 1990. Built to a high standard, the modern track features floodlighting and dedicated facilities for a wide range of field events. Today, it is used by local athletics clubs, schools and the wider community, including Brunel University London AC and Team Hounslow AC.

tracks.name: London Stadium

mapEmbed.title: London Stadium location map

tracks.description: London Stadium is a landmark 400m athletics venue in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, Stratford. Built for the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games, it staged the Olympic athletics programme and later hosted the 2017 World Athletics Championships and World Para Athletics Championships. The stadium has a distinctive dual life: it is the regular home of West Ham United during the football season, while in summer its adaptable lower-tier seating is reconfigured to reveal the track for major athletics meetings. It hosts the annual London Athletics Meet, the London leg of the Wanda Diamond League, bringing the world’s leading athletes back to the Olympic stage. With nine lanes and facilities for the full range of track and field events, it is one of Britain’s most significant athletics venues.
